answer: The cheapest real defence: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because zephyr only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, plume is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any velvet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
